conflicts.meeting_title: Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education Meeting
conflicts.issue: Racial/Socioeconomic Integration Strategy and State Voucher Threats Under DPS Growing Together
conflicts.summary: During the Growing Together briefing, commissioners and school board members debated how aggressively the new five-region elementary model should balance neighborhood walk zones against socioeconomic diversity and retaining affluent/white families amid North Carolina's expansion of universal Opportunity Scholarship vouchers.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prioritize equitable neighborhood walk-zone access and targeted investments in historically underserved schools while countering family flight and voucher losses through visible program quality across all five regions.
side_a_arguments: Neighborhood schools must be strengthened with Arts, Global Languages, and STEM programming so families remain in public schools rather than exiting to charters or private vouchers.
State budget projections estimate $6.4 million in annual DPS losses by 2026-27 as voucher uptake grows from 945 to over 2,600 students.
conflicts.side_b_position: Scrutinize whether the 50% walk-zone / 50% lottery balance and geographic boundaries will inadvertently deepen racial and socioeconomic segregation as new schools open.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners questioned whether walk-zone concentrations could re-segregate certain campuses without active diversity monitoring and accessible magnet transportation.
Requested longitudinal demographic tracking to evaluate whether student assignment shifts preserve county-wide integration goals.
conflicts.resolution: Informational joint discussion concluded without formal action; DPS staff committed to monitoring enrollment demographics, launching magnet/application lotteries in January 2024, and returning with implementation updates.

meetings.title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | Nov 17, 2023 | 9:00AM
meetings.executive_summary: At the quarterly joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (BOCC) and the DPS Board of Education, Chair Bettina Umstead presided over public comment, academic data reporting, universal free school meals discussions, and early childhood updates. The joint boards voted unanimously to move public comment to the start of the agenda and approve the August 15, 2023 joint minutes, then heard speakers advocate for universal free school lunches and urge pausing the relocated Durham School of the Arts (DSA) capital project over doubled costs and equity concerns for seven elementary projects. DPS Research & Accountability staff reported 2022-23 academic gains including ranking second in North Carolina in overall grade-level proficiency, achieving the highest cohort graduation rate since 2016, and leading peer districts with 88.2% of schools meeting or exceeding growth. Board members and commissioners also discussed Title I/CEP funding trade-offs for universal free meals, cultural meal inclusivity, and pre-K expansion at Murray-Massenburg Elementary before agreeing to reschedule 2024 meeting conflicts.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Amendment, and Approval of August 15, 2023 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead welcomed the joint BOCC and DPS Board of Education audience and Multilingual Resource Center interpreters. The joint boards voted unanimously to move public comment to the beginning of the agenda and approved the August 15, 2023 joint meeting minutes on a motion by Commissioner Brenda Howerton seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Universal Free Meals and Durham School of the Arts (DSA) Capital Costs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters—including Jeremy Bergren, a Durham CAN Poverty Team leader/Southern Durham parent, and DPS parents—advocated for universal free school meals and highlighted barriers facing immigrant and seasonal-worker families in completing online meal applications. Other speakers urged DPS and the county to pause and reconsider the move-DSA capital project due to doubled construction costs, arguing that financing a new DSA threatens funding and timelines for seven elementary school projects and repairs across the district.

agenda_items.title: DPS Student Academic Data Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga, Director of Data Integration Nelson Surles, and Director of Accountability and State Assessments Nathan Hester presented 2022-23 academic data. Highlights included a 64.9% composite in grades 5 and 8 science, a 20.2 percentage point gain among American Indian students, second place statewide in overall grade-level proficiency behind Chapel Hill-Carrboro, the highest cohort graduation rate since 2016, and 88.2% of schools meeting or exceeding growth.

agenda_items.title: Universal Free Meals, Nutrition Quality, and Title I/CEP Funding Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joint board members—including Alexandra Valladares and Millicent Rogers—questioned staff on meal utilization data, fresh produce options introduced by Child Nutrition Director Jim Keaton, Middle College app ordering, and cultural inclusivity such as labeling pork items. Officials explained the technical interactions between universal meals, CEP, and Title I position allotments ($50,000-$90,000 per school position), committing to bring back data and a potential budget ask for the upcoming year while affirming universal meal access as a shared goal.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Expansion Update, 2024 Joint Meeting Schedule, and Additional Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Chappelle reported local county dollars fund 653 preschool seats at roughly 92% enrollment and confirmed two pre-K classrooms are on track to open at the new Murray-Massenburg Elementary School following two added at Lyons Farm. Chair Umstead asked clerks to reschedule February and August 2024 joint meeting conflicts, and remaining public commenters spoke in favor of the new DSA building and accessible free-meal outreach before the meeting adjourned.

meetings.title: Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Board of Education Chair Bettina Umstead co-convened the August 15, 2023 Joint BOCC/BOE Meeting (with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs presiding for the final 15 minutes after Chair Howerton departed at 01:56:50). Durham Public Schools officials presented a multi-year Operational Services Life Safety Plan identifying a $2.6 million shortfall and ~$500,000 in annual maintenance needs across aging schools, followed by an in-depth Growing Together Initiative briefing outlining five new elementary regions, 50/50 neighborhood walk-zone and lottery application seats, K-12 Arts/Global Languages/STEM pathways, and $18 million in MacKenzie Scott philanthropy. Board members from both bodies engaged in candid discussion regarding racial and socioeconomic integration, retaining white and middle-class families, and an estimated $6.4 million annual DPS revenue loss from North Carolina Opportunity Scholarship expansion by 2026, before receiving back-to-school hiring updates showing 5.8% teacher vacancies, 68 bus driver openings, and the $90 million new Northern High School opening; no formal votes were taken.

agenda_items.title: Welcome and DPS Operational Services Life Safety Plan Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOCC Chair Brenda A. Howerton and BOE Chair Bettina Umstead opened the joint meeting, turning the floor to DPS COO Larry Johnson, Facilities Executive Director Frederick Davis, and Durham County Fire Marshal Chief Chris Shepard to present the Life Safety Plan. Officials reported that fire and life-safety inspections across aging facilities required a three-to-five-year remediation plan covering fire barriers, rated doors, dampers, and egress signage, estimating $4.3 million in identified projects plus ~$2.5 million TBD (leaving a $2.6 million gap after $1.7 million in ESSER funds) alongside roughly $500,000 in recurring annual upkeep. Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Heidi Carter praised the collaborative preventive safety inventory.

agenda_items.title: DPS Growing Together Initiative Update (Elementary Regions, Magnets, and Equity Strategy)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Deputy Superintendent Dr. Debbie Pittman, Executive Director Matthew Palmer, and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga presented implementation of the 'Growing Together' student assignment plan launching in 2024-25 (with secondary updates in 2025-26), establishing five geographic elementary regions, K-12 Arts/Global Languages/STEM theme alignment, transitioning School for Creative Studies to grades 6-8, and splitting application school access into 50% neighborhood walk-zone and 50% lottery seats backed by $18 million from MacKenzie Scott's gift. Commissioners and school board members engaged in extensive dialogue over building community buy-in across all demographics, reducing transportation bottlenecks, and combating an estimated $6.4 million annual loss to expanded state Opportunity Scholarship vouchers by 2026-27.

agenda_items.title: Back-to-School Readiness, Educator Recruitment/Retention, and Northern High School Opening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS officials Dr. Stacey Stewart, Dr. Alverez Lassiter, and Frederick Davis briefed both boards on back-to-school projections (31,044 expected traditional-calendar and year-round students), workforce metrics showing instructional vacancies down to 5.8% (4.9% overall) alongside 68 ongoing bus driver vacancies, and educator housing collaborations including Self-Help Credit Union's South Square townhomes and Duke TeachHouse. Chair Howerton departed at 01:56:50, passing the gavel to Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, as Davis showcased the opening of the $90 million new Northern High School (ahead of a September 14 ribbon cutting); members accepted the Durham Pre-K update as written and adjourned without public comments at 02:11:53.

meetings.title: BOCC/BOE Joint Quarterly Meeting | May 16, 2023 | 9:00AM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners met in a joint quarterly session focused exclusively on youth mental health supports following the May 15 community vigil at the Bull. After removing a planned closed session on safety and security to consult legal counsel and unanimously approving the January 31, 2023 joint meeting minutes, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga thanked County Manager Kimberly Sowell for recommending 100% of DPS's needs-based budget request and announced the upcoming departures of Dr. Julius Monk and Chip Sudderth. DPS Student Support Services and the Durham Public Schools Foundation presented data on counselor (1:274) and social worker (1:805) ratios, 10 ESSER-funded mental health counselors, restorative practices, and the three-year Whole Schools wellness initiative. Officials from both boards discussed sustaining mental health positions after the ESSER cliff, reviving co-located Alliance Behavioral Health services, and expanding youth conflict-resolution and trauma-informed educator training.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Approval of January 31, 2023 Joint Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the joint BOCC/BOE meeting to order and gained consensus to remove a scheduled closed session on safety and security pending legal review. BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton moved and Commissioner Burns seconded approval of the January 31, 2023 joint meeting minutes with a minor correction ('maternal health' instead of 'internal health'), passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Remarks on County Budget and Leadership Transitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga recognized departing cabinet members Dr. Julius Monk (moving to Guilford County) and longtime communications chief Chip Sudderth. He also thanked County Manager Kimberly Sowell for recommending 100% of DPS's FY 2023-24 needs-based budget request and urged county commissioners to support it.

agenda_items.title: DPS Student Mental Health and Wellness Supports Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS staff presented district-wide mental health infrastructure, including at least one full-time counselor in every school (1:274 ratio toward a 1:250 goal), a 1:805 social worker ratio, 10 ESSER-funded mental health counselors, restorative practices, and bilingual support needs. Board members and county commissioners discussed post-ESSER sustainability, co-located mental health partnerships with Alliance, public health nurse recruitment, youth conflict resolution, and trauma-informed TILT training.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Foundation: Whole Schools Mental Health Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Foundation representatives presented the three-year Whole Schools wellness pilot with Dr. Max Perry, highlighting teacher wellness spaces, community wellness ambassadors, and sustainable district-wide coaching hubs. Officials discussed integrating Foundation trainings with existing district teams and Alliance Behavioral Health before adjourning at 02:05:06.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 31, 2023 Joint BOCC/BOE Meeting Minutes (as Corrected)
votes.notes: Joint vote of both BOCC and BOE members; mover and seconder were BOCC members Chair Brenda Howerton and Commissioner Burns.
votes.discussion_detail: BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton moved approval of the January 31, 2023 joint meeting minutes, seconded by Commissioner Burns. Commissioner Jacobs requested correcting 'internal health' to 'maternal health' on page 3, and the joint bodies approved the amended minutes unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-Board of Education Meeting for January 31, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of County Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education held a joint meeting on January 31, 2023, opening with approval of the November 29, 2022 joint meeting minutes. DPS Chief Financial Officer Paul LeSieur presented a detailed accounting of approximately $158 million in federal COVID relief (ESSER I, II, and III) funding used for summer learning, temporary school support staff, IT cybersecurity, nutrition, transportation, and 13 workstation technicians, while warning of the upcoming fiscal cliff and noting five completed federal/state audits. Officials then reviewed DPS's early draft FY2024 baseline budget—discussing local funding for bus driver pay above $18 per hour, implementation of the classified staff salary study, teacher supplement increases ($833), ~$5 million in lapsed salaries, state Leandro underfunding, and tax pressures from the recently passed school bond. A DPS parent closed public comments with a five-point advocacy primer citing North Carolina's low national rankings in teacher pay and per-pupil funding, and commissioners praised the School Board for completing redistricting and adopting a new LGBTQI student policy.

agenda_items.title: Opening Quorum Check and Approval of November 29, 2022 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members waited briefly to confirm quorum, with Chair Brenda A. Howerton noting she would have to depart early and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs would cover. Once convened, a motion to approve the November 29, 2022 joint meeting minutes was moved, seconded, and approved.

agenda_items.title: DPS Federal COVID-19 / ESSER Funding Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur walked through the district's CARES/ESSER I, CRRSA/ESSER II, and ARP/ESSER III funds (including $104.57 million in ESSER III and ~$158 million across major pots) deployed for summer learning, temporary school positions, student support services, IT cybersecurity, nutrition, transportation, and 13 workstation technicians supporting 1:1 devices. Officials discussed which recurring needs—such as the 13 technicians—would require local budget absorption once ESSER expires, and LeSieur noted DPS had already undergone five audits and monitoring visits through Q2 of FY23.

agenda_items.title: Draft FY24 DPS Budget, Classified/Teacher Pay, and Leandro Advocacy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Officials discussed DPS's early draft FY24 baseline budget, highlighting local funds supporting bus driver pay above $18 per hour, classified salary study implementation (contingent on both County and State funding), an $833 teacher supplement increase, and ~$5 million in lapsed salaries used to cover gaps. Participants discussed North Carolina's failure to fund Leandro obligations and how joint county-school advocacy could educate parents on state underfunding. Commissioners requested staff vacancy figures, charter/homeschool enrollment data, and reminded members of potential tax impacts from the recently approved school bond alongside over $10 million in county ARPA investments supporting families and the DPS Foundation.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments and Closing Remarks on Redistricting and LGBTQI Student Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS parent Karthik Sundaramurthy shared a five-point advocacy primer covering competitive compensation, teacher pipeline, student mental health, readiness, and remedial plans, citing statistics that North Carolina ranks 38th in teacher pay, 48th in per-pupil spending, and 50th in funding effort. In closing remarks before adjournment, a commissioner congratulated the School Board on completing difficult school redistricting decisions and praised DPS's new LGBTQI student policy.

votes.notes: Joint meeting of BOCC and DPS Board of Education; individual roll-call votes were not read.
votes.discussion_detail: A member moved and seconded approval of the November 29, 2022 joint meeting minutes, and the motion was approved.
